articles.title: 3-day memorial run from Toronto to Ottawa kicks off to honour 7 fallen police officers
articles.summary: About 300 runners took off from Queen's Park this morning for a memorial run to Ottawa in honour of police officers who died in the line of duty this past year, including Toronto Const. Marc Pinizzotto, OPP Sgt. Brandon Malcolm and OPP Const. Tarun Bali.

articles.title: Bonnie Crombie wants TTC Line 2 subway extended to Mississauga: ‘Should be part of that conversation’
articles.summary: Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie is putting transit and gridlock at the centre of her campaign, unveiling an ambitious transportation plan that includes bringing Toronto’s subway system into Mississauga. articles.title: Ontario hospital plans to cut hundreds of jobs amid province-directed budget plan
articles.summary: TORONTO — Hamilton Health Sciences is planning to eliminate more than 400 jobs, a move it is directly tying to provincial marching orders to balance budgets that have seen other hospitals across the province make similar cuts.

articles.title: PWHL to host all-star event for first time in Toronto
articles.summary: The Professional Women’s Hockey League (PWHL) will host an all-star event for the first time on March 7, 2027 in Toronto. The league says the four-team three-on-three tournament will be held at Scotiabank Arena.   The PWHL all-stars will compete in a round-robin format using 10-player rosters of six forwards, three defenders and one goaltender. articles.title: Maple Leaf hopes protein craze will help drive comeback for Yves Veggie brand
articles.summary: MISSISSAUGA — Maple Leaf Foods is betting the protein-maxxing trend will help drive a comeback for its Yves Veggie Cuisine brand.

articles.summary: A pedestrian was rushed to a hospital with serious injuries Thursday morning after getting hit by a vehicle in Richmond Hill, according to police. articles.title: Peel police investigate suspected arson after 2 tow truck fires in Mississauga
articles.summary: Peel police are investigating a suspected arson after two tow trucks were found on fire in Mississauga Thursday morning.

articles.title: ‘We shouldn't have to beg,’ says chief of First Nation facing decades of mercury poisoning in Ontario
articles.summary: Grassy Narrows First Nation and Wabaseemoong Independent Nations continue to seek justice from the provincial and federal governments over decades of mercury poisoning caused by contamination that dates back to the 1960s and '70s. The First Nations' River Run Rally drew about 9,000 people to downtown Toronto on Wednesday. Here's what they want to see happen.

articles.title: What Mark Carney’s new plan could mean for Pearson travellers
articles.summary: It’s been a week since Prime Minister Mark Carney said he wants private investors to take over operations at Canada's four largest airports, including Toronto's Pearson airport. And there are still questions around how it could affect travellers. CBC's Talia Ricci breaks down what we know.

articles.title: Police investigating fire at Leslieville store selling Hells Angels merchandise
articles.summary: Toronto police are investigating a fire that broke out Wednesday at a Leslieville retail store connected to the Hells Angels. They say the fire is now considered suspicious and they are still trying to determine the cause.
